questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the thermal decomposition of lithium nitrate and sodium nitrate?
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the thermal decomposition of lithium nitrate and sodium nitrate?
options: Lithium nitrate evolves a mixture of two gases, while sodium nitrate evolves only one gas.
Both nitrates release a brown gas upon heating.
Both nitrates leave behind a solid metal oxide as the residue.
Lithium nitrate releases only one gas upon heating.
questions.solution:
The thermal decomposition of lithium nitrate and sodium nitrate proceeds as follows:

$4\text{LiNO}_3 \to 2\text{Li}_2\text{O} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$
$2\text{NaNO}_3 \to 2\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{O}_2$

Lithium nitrate evolves a mixture of two gases ($\text{NO}_2$ which is a brown gas, and $\text{O}_2$), whereas sodium nitrate evolves only one gas ($\text{O}_2$). Also, lithium nitrate leaves behind a metal oxide ($\text{Li}_2\text{O}$), while sodium nitrate leaves behind a metal nitrite ($\text{NaNO}_2$). Thus, the statement that lithium nitrate evolves a mixture of two gases, while sodium nitrate evolves only one gas, is correct.

Answer: Lithium nitrate evolves a mixture of two gases, while sodium nitrate evolves only one gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the following oxides formed by elements from the s and p blocks: $\text{SO}_3$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{CaO}$, and $\text{K}_2\text{O}$. Which of the following represents the correct increasing order of their basic character?
questions.question: Consider the following oxides formed by elements from the s and p blocks: $\text{SO}_3$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{CaO}$, and $\text{K}_2\text{O}$. Which of the following represents the correct increasing order of their basic character?
questions.solution:
The basic character of an oxide is directly related to the metallic character of its central element. Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period from left to right.

The central elements are Sulphur (S), Aluminium (Al), Calcium (Ca), and Potassium (K).
Sulphur is a non-metal, so $\text{SO}_3$ is an acidic oxide.
Aluminium is a metal/metalloid, and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is an amphoteric oxide.
Calcium is a Group 2 metal, so $\text{CaO}$ is a basic oxide.
Potassium is a Group 1 metal, so $\text{K}_2\text{O}$ is a strongly basic oxide.

The increasing order of metallic character is $\text{S} < \text{Al} < \text{Ca} < \text{K}$.
Therefore, the increasing order of basic character of their oxides follows the same trend: $\text{SO}_3 < \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 < \text{CaO} < \text{K}_2\text{O}$.

Answer: $\text{SO}_3 < \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 < \text{CaO} < \text{K}_2\text{O}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A certain amount of energy is completely consumed to convert a sample of gaseous beryllium atoms into $\text{Be}^{2+}\text{(g)}$ ions. If the total energy supplied is $13.28 \text{ kJ}$, the mass of the beryllium sample ionized is _______ $\text{mg}$.

[Given: First and second ionization enthalpies of Be are $899 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $1757 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. Molar mass of Be $= 9 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$]
questions.question:
A certain amount of energy is completely consumed to convert a sample of gaseous beryllium atoms into $\text{Be}^{2+}\text{(g)}$ ions. If the total energy supplied is $13.28 \text{ kJ}$, the mass of the beryllium sample ionized is _______ $\text{mg}$.

[Given: First and second ionization enthalpies of Be are $899 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $1757 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. Molar mass of Be $= 9 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
The conversion of $\text{Be(g)}$ to $\text{Be}^{2+}\text{(g)}$ requires the removal of two electrons.

Total ionization energy required per mole $= IE_1 + IE_2$
$= 899 + 1757 = 2656 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Total energy supplied $= 13.28 \text{ kJ}$

Number of moles of Be ionized $= \dfrac{13.28 \text{ kJ}}{2656 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}} = 0.005 \text{ mol}$

Mass of Be in grams $= 0.005 \text{ mol} \times 9 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.045 \text{ g}$

Mass in milligrams $= 0.045 \times 1000 = 45 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $45$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two different alkali metals $M_1$ and $M_2$ form nitrates $M_1\text{NO}_3$ and $M_2\text{NO}_3$. Upon strong heating, $M_1\text{NO}_3$ evolves a brown gas along with a colourless gas, whereas $M_2\text{NO}_3$ evolves only a colourless gas. Identify $M_1$ and $M_2$ from the given options.
questions.question: Two different alkali metals $M_1$ and $M_2$ form nitrates $M_1\text{NO}_3$ and $M_2\text{NO}_3$. Upon strong heating, $M_1\text{NO}_3$ evolves a brown gas along with a colourless gas, whereas $M_2\text{NO}_3$ evolves only a colourless gas. Identify $M_1$ and $M_2$ from the given options.
questions.solution:
Alkali metal nitrates decompose on heating. Except lithium, all other alkali metal nitrates decompose to give the corresponding metal nitrite and oxygen (a colourless gas).
$2M\text{NO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2M\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$ (where $M = \text{Na, K, Rb, Cs}$)

Lithium nitrate exhibits anomalous behaviour and decomposes to give lithium oxide, nitrogen dioxide (a brown gas), and oxygen (a colourless gas).
$4\text{LiNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{Li}_2\text{O} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$

Since $M_1\text{NO}_3$ evolves a brown gas, $M_1$ must be $\text{Li}$.
Since $M_2\text{NO}_3$ evolves only a colourless gas, $M_2$ can be $\text{Na}$, $\text{K}$, $\text{Rb}$, or $\text{Cs}$.
Therefore, the correct pair is $M_1 = \text{Li}$ and $M_2 = \text{K}$.

Answer: $M_1 = \text{Li}, M_2 = \text{K}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.


List I (Ion)List II (Hydration enthalpy in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$)
(A) $\text{Na}^+$(I) $-1921$
(B) $\text{Rb}^+$(II) $-1305$
(C) $\text{Mg}^{2+}$(III) $-406$
(D) $\text{Ba}^{2+}$(IV) $-293$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Match List I with List II.


List I (Ion)List II (Hydration enthalpy in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$)
(A) $\text{Na}^+$(I) $-1921$
(B) $\text{Rb}^+$(II) $-1305$
(C) $\text{Mg}^{2+}$(III) $-406$
(D) $\text{Ba}^{2+}$(IV) $-293$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The magnitude of hydration enthalpy depends on the charge density of the ion. Alkaline earth metal ions (Group 2) have a higher charge and smaller size compared to alkali metal ions (Group 1) of the same period, leading to much more negative hydration enthalpies.

Thus, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ will have the more negative values ($-1921$ and $-1305\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$).

Within a group, as the ionic size increases down the group, the degree of hydration decreases, and so does the magnitude of hydration enthalpy.

For Group 2: $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ is smaller than $\text{Ba}^{2+}$, so $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ has a hydration enthalpy of $-1921\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ has $-1305\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

For Group 1: $\text{Na}^+$ is smaller than $\text{Rb}^+$, so $\text{Na}^+$ has a hydration enthalpy of $-406\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\text{Rb}^+$ has $-293\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The standard hydration enthalpies of four alkaline earth metal ions, namely $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{Sr}^{2+}$, and $\text{Ba}^{2+}$, are given in a random order as $-1305 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, $-1921 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, $-1577 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, and $-1443 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

The hydration enthalpy of the $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion is:
questions.question:
The standard hydration enthalpies of four alkaline earth metal ions, namely $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{Sr}^{2+}$, and $\text{Ba}^{2+}$, are given in a random order as $-1305 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, $-1921 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, $-1577 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, and $-1443 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

The hydration enthalpy of the $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ion is:
questions.solution:
The magnitude of hydration enthalpy depends on the size of the ion. Smaller ions have a higher charge density and thus undergo more extensive hydration, releasing more energy (more negative hydration enthalpy).

The order of ionic radii for the given alkaline earth metals is $\text{Mg}^{2+} < \text{Ca}^{2+} < \text{Sr}^{2+} < \text{Ba}^{2+}$.

Therefore, the magnitude of hydration enthalpy follows the reverse order: $\text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Ca}^{2+} > \text{Sr}^{2+} > \text{Ba}^{2+}$.

Since $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ is the smallest ion among the four, it will have the most negative hydration enthalpy. Matching the given values, the hydration enthalpy of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ is $-1921 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $-1921 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the strongest reducing agent among alkali metals in aqueous solution and in the gaseous state, respectively.
questions.question: Identify the strongest reducing agent among alkali metals in aqueous solution and in the gaseous state, respectively.
questions.solution:
The reducing power of a metal is highly dependent on the medium in which the reaction occurs.

In aqueous solution, reducing power is governed by the standard electrode potential, which is a combined effect of sublimation enthalpy, ionization enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy. Lithium ($\text{Li}$) has the most negative standard reduction potential due to its exceptionally high hydration enthalpy, which overcomes its high ionization enthalpy. Thus, $\text{Li}$ is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution.

In the gaseous state, hydration enthalpy plays no role. The reducing power depends solely on the tendency of the isolated gaseous atom to lose an electron, which is inversely related to the ionization enthalpy. Cesium ($\text{Cs}$) has the lowest ionization enthalpy among the stable alkali metals due to its large atomic size, making it the easiest to oxidize. Thus, $\text{Cs}$ is the strongest reducing agent in the gaseous phase.

Therefore, the correct pair is $\text{Li}$ and $\text{Cs}$.

Answer: $\text{Li}$ and $\text{Cs}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the alkaline earth metals $\text{Be}, \text{Mg}, \text{Ca}, \text{Sr}$, and $\text{Ba}$. The number of metals that impart a characteristic colour to the Bunsen flame AND have a standard reduction potential $E^{\circ}(\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M})$ more negative than $-2.85 \text{ V}$ is
questions.question: Consider the alkaline earth metals $\text{Be}, \text{Mg}, \text{Ca}, \text{Sr}$, and $\text{Ba}$. The number of metals that impart a characteristic colour to the Bunsen flame AND have a standard reduction potential $E^{\circ}(\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M})$ more negative than $-2.85 \text{ V}$ is
questions.solution:
The alkaline earth metals that impart a characteristic colour to the Bunsen flame are $\text{Ca}$ (brick red), $\text{Sr}$ (crimson), and $\text{Ba}$ (apple green). $\text{Be}$ and $\text{Mg}$ do not impart any colour due to their high ionization enthalpies.

The standard reduction potentials $E^{\circ}(\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M})$ for these metals are approximately:
$\text{Be} : -1.97 \text{ V}$
$\text{Mg} : -2.36 \text{ V}$
$\text{Ca} : -2.84 \text{ V}$
$\text{Sr} : -2.89 \text{ V}$
$\text{Ba} : -2.90 \text{ V}$

The metals with an $E^{\circ}$ value more negative than $-2.85 \text{ V}$ are $\text{Sr}$ and $\text{Ba}$.

Both $\text{Sr}$ and $\text{Ba}$ satisfy both conditions (imparting flame colour and having $E^{\circ} < -2.85 \text{ V}$).

Thus, the number of such metals is $2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $2$ moles of lithium nitrate and $2$ moles of potassium nitrate are heated separately in two different vessels until a constant weight is achieved. The ratio of the total moles of gaseous products formed from the decomposition of lithium nitrate to that from potassium nitrate is
questions.question: $2$ moles of lithium nitrate and $2$ moles of potassium nitrate are heated separately in two different vessels until a constant weight is achieved. The ratio of the total moles of gaseous products formed from the decomposition of lithium nitrate to that from potassium nitrate is
questions.solution:
The thermal decomposition of lithium nitrate is given by the balanced chemical equation:
$4\text{LiNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{Li}_2\text{O} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$
From the stoichiometry, $4$ moles of $\text{LiNO}_3$ produce $4 + 1 = 5$ moles of gaseous products ($\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$).
Therefore, $2$ moles of $\text{LiNO}_3$ will produce $\dfrac{5}{2} = 2.5$ moles of gaseous products.

The thermal decomposition of potassium nitrate is given by:
$2\text{KNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{KNO}_2 + \text{O}_2$
From the stoichiometry, $2$ moles of $\text{KNO}_3$ produce $1$ mole of gaseous product ($\text{O}_2$).

The required ratio of the total moles of gaseous products is:
$\text{Ratio} = \dfrac{2.5}{1} = \dfrac{5}{2} = 5 : 2$

Answer: $5 : 2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the alkali metals $\text{Li}, \text{Na}, \text{K}, \text{Rb}$, and $\text{Cs}$, the number of metals that form predominantly a superoxide upon heating in excess air AND have a density less than $1.0 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ is
questions.question: Among the alkali metals $\text{Li}, \text{Na}, \text{K}, \text{Rb}$, and $\text{Cs}$, the number of metals that form predominantly a superoxide upon heating in excess air AND have a density less than $1.0 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ is
questions.solution:
Alkali metals that form predominantly superoxides when heated in excess air are $\text{K}, \text{Rb}$, and $\text{Cs}$.

The densities of the given alkali metals are approximately:
$\text{Li} = 0.53 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$
$\text{Na} = 0.97 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$
$\text{K} = 0.86 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$
$\text{Rb} = 1.53 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$
$\text{Cs} = 1.90 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$

The metals with a density less than $1.0 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ are $\text{Li}, \text{Na}$, and $\text{K}$.

The only metal satisfying both conditions (forming a superoxide and having density $< 1.0 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$) is $\text{K}$.

Therefore, the number of such metals is $1$.

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element belonging to Group 1 of the periodic table forms a unipositive ion. In this ionic state, the ratio of the total number of p-electrons to the total number of s-electrons is exactly $2.4$. The atomic number of this element is
questions.question: An element belonging to Group 1 of the periodic table forms a unipositive ion. In this ionic state, the ratio of the total number of p-electrons to the total number of s-electrons is exactly $2.4$. The atomic number of this element is
questions.solution:
Let the element be $M$. Since it belongs to Group 1, its unipositive ion $M^{+}$ will have the stable electronic configuration of a noble gas.

Let us evaluate the ratio of p-electrons to s-electrons for the noble gas cores:
For $\text{Na}^{+}$ (Neon core): $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6}$. Number of s-electrons $= 4$, p-electrons $= 6$. Ratio $= \dfrac{6}{4} = 1.5$
For $\text{K}^{+}$ (Argon core): $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{2} 3p^{6}$. Number of s-electrons $= 6$, p-electrons $= 12$. Ratio $= \dfrac{12}{6} = 2.0$
For $\text{Rb}^{+}$ (Krypton core): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^{2} 4p^{6}$. Number of s-electrons $= 8$, p-electrons $= 18$. Ratio $= \dfrac{18}{8} = 2.25$
For $\text{Cs}^{+}$ (Xenon core): $[\text{Kr}] 4d^{10} 5s^{2} 5p^{6}$. Number of s-electrons $= 10$, p-electrons $= 24$. Ratio $= \dfrac{24}{10} = 2.4$

The ion $M^{+}$ has the Xenon core, which corresponds to $54$ electrons. Since it is a unipositive ion, the neutral atom $M$ has $54 + 1 = 55$ electrons. Therefore, the atomic number of the element is $55$.

Answer: $55$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the total energy required to convert a $11.5 \text{ g}$ solid piece of sodium metal completely into gaseous $\text{Na}^{+}$ ions. The total energy absorbed is _______ $\text{kJ}$.

[Given: Enthalpy of sublimation of Na $= 108 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, First ionization enthalpy of Na $= 496 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, Molar mass of Na $= 23 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$]
questions.question:
Calculate the total energy required to convert a $11.5 \text{ g}$ solid piece of sodium metal completely into gaseous $\text{Na}^{+}$ ions. The total energy absorbed is _______ $\text{kJ}$.

[Given: Enthalpy of sublimation of Na $= 108 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, First ionization enthalpy of Na $= 496 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, Molar mass of Na $= 23 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
The conversion of solid sodium to gaseous sodium ions involves two steps: sublimation of solid sodium to gaseous sodium atoms, followed by the ionization of gaseous sodium atoms.

Total energy required per mole $= \Delta_{sub}H + IE_1$
$= 108 + 496 = 604 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Number of moles of sodium $= \dfrac{11.5 \text{ g}}{23 \text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.5 \text{ mol}$

Total energy required for $0.5 \text{ mol}$ of Na $= 0.5 \text{ mol} \times 604 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = 302 \text{ kJ}$

Answer: $302$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element $\text{X}$ belongs to Group $2$ of the periodic table and possesses the highest first ionization enthalpy within its group. Element $\text{X}$ exhibits a diagonal relationship with an element $\text{Y}$ belonging to Group $13$. The identity of element $\text{Y}$ is
questions.question: An element $\text{X}$ belongs to Group $2$ of the periodic table and possesses the highest first ionization enthalpy within its group. Element $\text{X}$ exhibits a diagonal relationship with an element $\text{Y}$ belonging to Group $13$. The identity of element $\text{Y}$ is
questions.solution:
First ionization enthalpy decreases down a group due to an increase in atomic size. Therefore, the element with the highest first ionization enthalpy in Group $2$ is Beryllium ($\text{Be}$).

In the periodic table, the first element of Group $2$ ($\text{Be}$) shows a diagonal relationship with the second element of Group $13$.

Thus, Beryllium ($\text{Be}$) is diagonally related to Aluminum ($\text{Al}$).

Hence, the element $\text{Y}$ is $\text{Al}$.

Answer: $\text{Al}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkali metal compound contains an oxygen-based anion. According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the anion is paramagnetic and has a fractional bond order of 1.5. Which of the following is the correct formula of the compound?
questions.question: An alkali metal compound contains an oxygen-based anion. According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the anion is paramagnetic and has a fractional bond order of 1.5. Which of the following is the correct formula of the compound?
questions.solution:
The given anion is paramagnetic and has a bond order of 1.5.

Let us check the oxygen anions in the given compounds:
$\text{Li}_2\text{O}$ contains the oxide ion ($\text{O}^{2-}$), which is monoatomic and diamagnetic.
$\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$ and $\text{BaO}_2$ contain the peroxide ion ($\text{O}_2^{2-}$). The total number of electrons is 18. The bond order is $\dfrac{10 - 8}{2} = 1$. It has zero unpaired electrons, so it is diamagnetic.
$\text{KO}_2$ contains the superoxide ion ($\text{O}_2^{-}$). The total number of electrons is 17. The bond order is $\dfrac{10 - 7}{2} = 1.5$. It has one unpaired electron in the $\pi^{*}$ orbital, making it paramagnetic.

Thus, the compound is $\text{KO}_2$.

Answer: $\text{KO}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: One mole of $\text{LiNO}_3$ and one mole of $\text{NaNO}_3$ are heated separately in closed vessels until complete decomposition occurs. The ratio of the total moles of gases produced by $\text{LiNO}_3$ to the total moles of gases produced by $\text{NaNO}_3$ is:
questions.question: One mole of $\text{LiNO}_3$ and one mole of $\text{NaNO}_3$ are heated separately in closed vessels until complete decomposition occurs. The ratio of the total moles of gases produced by $\text{LiNO}_3$ to the total moles of gases produced by $\text{NaNO}_3$ is:
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equations for the thermal decomposition are:

$4\text{LiNO}_3 \to 2\text{Li}_2\text{O} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$
From the equation, $4$ moles of $\text{LiNO}_3$ produce $4 + 1 = 5$ moles of gas.
Therefore, $1$ mole of $\text{LiNO}_3$ produces $\dfrac{5}{4} = 1.25$ moles of gas.

$2\text{NaNO}_3 \to 2\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{O}_2$
From the equation, $2$ moles of $\text{NaNO}_3$ produce $1$ mole of gas.
Therefore, $1$ mole of $\text{NaNO}_3$ produces $\dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5$ moles of gas.

The required ratio is $\dfrac{1.25}{0.5} = \dfrac{5/4}{1/2} = \dfrac{5}{2}$, which is $5:2$.

Answer: $5:2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An alkaline earth metal oxide $A$ and an oxide of nitrogen $B$ react with water. $A$ forms ONLY compound $X$, and $B$ forms ONLY compound $Y$. $X$ is the hydroxide of the Group 2 metal belonging to the $4^{\text{th}}$ period. $Y$ is an oxoacid of nitrogen in which nitrogen is in a $+5$ oxidation state.

The total number of atoms in one molecule of $A$ and one molecule of $B$ is ______
questions.question:
An alkaline earth metal oxide $A$ and an oxide of nitrogen $B$ react with water. $A$ forms ONLY compound $X$, and $B$ forms ONLY compound $Y$. $X$ is the hydroxide of the Group 2 metal belonging to the $4^{\text{th}}$ period. $Y$ is an oxoacid of nitrogen in which nitrogen is in a $+5$ oxidation state.

The total number of atoms in one molecule of $A$ and one molecule of $B$ is ______
questions.solution:
The Group 2 metal belonging to the $4^{\text{th}}$ period is Calcium (Ca).
Thus, the hydroxide $X$ is $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$.
The alkaline earth metal oxide $A$ that reacts with water to form $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is $\text{CaO}$.
The atomicity (number of atoms per molecule) of $\text{CaO}$ is $1 + 1 = 2$.

The oxoacid of nitrogen $Y$ with nitrogen in the $+5$ oxidation state is nitric acid, $\text{HNO}_3$.
The oxide of nitrogen $B$ that reacts with water to form ONLY $\text{HNO}_3$ is dinitrogen pentoxide, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$.
$\text{N}_2\text{O}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{HNO}_3$
The atomicity of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is $2 + 5 = 7$.

The total number of atoms in one molecule of $A$ and one molecule of $B$ is $2 + 7 = 9$.

Answer: $9$

questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

(A) $N_2O$(I) Basic
(B) $Al_2O_3$(II) Acidic
(C) $SrO$(III) Amphoteric
(D) $SO_3$(IV) Neutral

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Oxides)List II (Nature)
(A) $N_2O$(I) Basic
(B) $Al_2O_3$(II) Acidic
(C) $SrO$(III) Amphoteric
(D) $SO_3$(IV) Neutral

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
$N_2O$ is a neutral oxide of nitrogen.

$Al_2O_3$ is a well-known amphoteric oxide, reacting with both acids and bases.

$SrO$ is an alkaline earth metal oxide, which is basic in nature.

$SO_3$ is a non-metal oxide in a high oxidation state, making it strongly acidic.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkaline earth metal ions exhibits the highest ionic mobility in an aqueous solution?
questions.question: Which of the following alkaline earth metal ions exhibits the highest ionic mobility in an aqueous solution?
questions.solution:
The ionic mobility of an ion in an aqueous solution is inversely proportional to its hydrated radius. A larger hydrated radius leads to lower mobility due to increased viscous drag.

The extent of hydration of an ion depends on its bare ionic size. Smaller ions have a higher charge density, leading to a greater degree of hydration and a larger hydrated radius.

The bare ionic radii of the given ions increase down the group: $\text{Be}^{2+} < \text{Mg}^{2+} < \text{Ca}^{2+} < \text{Sr}^{2+}$.

Consequently, the hydrated radii follow the reverse order: $\text{Be}^{2+}_{(\text{aq})} > \text{Mg}^{2+}_{(\text{aq})} > \text{Ca}^{2+}_{(\text{aq})} > \text{Sr}^{2+}_{(\text{aq})}$.

Since $\text{Sr}^{2+}$ has the smallest hydrated radius among the given options, it will exhibit the highest ionic mobility in an aqueous solution.

Answer: $\text{Sr}^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A trivalent anion, $X^{3-}$, is isoelectronic with a noble gas. If this noble gas contains exactly $18$ p-electrons, the total number of s-electrons present in the ground state of the neutral atom $X$ is
questions.question: A trivalent anion, $X^{3-}$, is isoelectronic with a noble gas. If this noble gas contains exactly $18$ p-electrons, the total number of s-electrons present in the ground state of the neutral atom $X$ is
questions.solution:
First, identify the noble gas. The p-subshells are filled in the order $2p$, $3p$, $4p$, etc. Each fully filled p-subshell holds $6$ electrons.
For the noble gas to have exactly $18$ p-electrons, it must have fully filled $2p$, $3p$, and $4p$ subshells ($6 + 6 + 6 = 18$).
The electronic configuration of this noble gas is $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{2} 3p^{6} 4s^{2} 3d^{10} 4p^{6}$, which corresponds to Krypton ($Z = 36$).

The trivalent anion $X^{3-}$ is isoelectronic with Krypton, meaning $X^{3-}$ has $36$ electrons.
The neutral atom $X$ must therefore have $36 - 3 = 33$ electrons.

The electronic configuration of the neutral atom $X$ ($Z = 33$) is:
$1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{2} 3p^{6} 4s^{2} 3d^{10} 4p^{3}$

The s-electrons in this configuration are found in the $1s$, $2s$, $3s$, and $4s$ orbitals. Each contains $2$ electrons.
Total number of s-electrons $= 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8$.

Answer: $8$

questions.q: Let $x$ be the number of electrons present in the $\pi^{*}$ (pi-antibonding) molecular orbitals of the anion in $\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$, and $y$ be the number of electrons present in the $\pi^{*}$ molecular orbitals of the anion in $\text{KO}_2$. What is the value of $(x + y)$ and the magnetic nature of the anion present in $\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$?
questions.question: Let $x$ be the number of electrons present in the $\pi^{*}$ (pi-antibonding) molecular orbitals of the anion in $\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$, and $y$ be the number of electrons present in the $\pi^{*}$ molecular orbitals of the anion in $\text{KO}_2$. What is the value of $(x + y)$ and the magnetic nature of the anion present in $\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$?
questions.solution:
The anion in $\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$ is the peroxide ion ($\text{O}_2^{2-}$).
Total number of electrons in $\text{O}_2^{2-}$ = 18.
The molecular orbital configuration is: $\sigma 1s^2, \sigma^{*} 1s^2, \sigma 2s^2, \sigma^{*} 2s^2, \sigma 2p_z^2, \pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2, \pi^{*} 2p_x^2 = \pi^{*} 2p_y^2$.
Number of electrons in $\pi^{*}$ orbitals, $x = 4$.
Since all electrons are paired, the peroxide ion is diamagnetic.

The anion in $\text{KO}_2$ is the superoxide ion ($\text{O}_2^{-}$).
Total number of electrons in $\text{O}_2^{-}$ = 17.
The molecular orbital configuration is: $\sigma 1s^2, \sigma^{*} 1s^2, \sigma 2s^2, \sigma^{*} 2s^2, \sigma 2p_z^2, \pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2, \pi^{*} 2p_x^2 = \pi^{*} 2p_y^1$.
Number of electrons in $\pi^{*}$ orbitals, $y = 3$.

Therefore, $x + y = 4 + 3 = 7$.
The anion in $\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$ is diamagnetic.

Answer: 7, diamagnetic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Among the following nitrates, the number of nitrates that evolve a brown coloured gas on strong heating is ________.

$\text{LiNO}_3, \text{NaNO}_3, \text{KNO}_3, \text{RbNO}_3, \text{Mg(NO}_3)_2, \text{Ca(NO}_3)_2, \text{Sr(NO}_3)_2, \text{Ba(NO}_3)_2$
questions.question:
Among the following nitrates, the number of nitrates that evolve a brown coloured gas on strong heating is ________.

$\text{LiNO}_3, \text{NaNO}_3, \text{KNO}_3, \text{RbNO}_3, \text{Mg(NO}_3)_2, \text{Ca(NO}_3)_2, \text{Sr(NO}_3)_2, \text{Ba(NO}_3)_2$
questions.solution:
The thermal decomposition of s-block nitrates follows specific trends:

Group 1 nitrates (except Lithium) decompose on heating to give the corresponding metal nitrite and oxygen gas (which is colourless).
$2\text{MNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{MNO}_2 + \text{O}_2$ (where $\text{M} = \text{Na}, \text{K}, \text{Rb}$)

Group 2 nitrates and Lithium nitrate (due to its anomalous behaviour and diagonal relationship with Magnesium) decompose to give the corresponding metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide gas, and oxygen gas.
$4\text{LiNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{Li}_2\text{O} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$
$2\text{M(NO}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$ (where $\text{M} = \text{Mg}, \text{Ca}, \text{Sr}, \text{Ba}$)

Nitrogen dioxide ($\text{NO}_2$) is a brown coloured gas.

Therefore, the nitrates that evolve a brown gas are $\text{LiNO}_3, \text{Mg(NO}_3)_2, \text{Ca(NO}_3)_2, \text{Sr(NO}_3)_2$, and $\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2$.

Total number of such nitrates = $5$.

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An alkali metal $M$ on combustion in excess oxygen forms a major product $X$ which is paramagnetic. $X$ reacts with water to form a base $Y$, a compound $Z$, and a diatomic gas $W$.

The sum of the atomicity (total number of atoms per molecule) of $X$, $Y$, $Z$, and $W$ is ______
questions.question:
An alkali metal $M$ on combustion in excess oxygen forms a major product $X$ which is paramagnetic. $X$ reacts with water to form a base $Y$, a compound $Z$, and a diatomic gas $W$.

The sum of the atomicity (total number of atoms per molecule) of $X$, $Y$, $Z$, and $W$ is ______
questions.solution:
Alkali metals like K, Rb, and Cs react with excess oxygen to form superoxides as the major product. Superoxides contain the $\text{O}_2^-$ ion, which has an unpaired electron and is paramagnetic.
Thus, $X$ is a superoxide with the formula $M\text{O}_2$.
The atomicity of $X$ ($M\text{O}_2$) is $1 + 2 = 3$.

The hydrolysis of a superoxide proceeds as follows:
$2M\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2M\text{OH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + \text{O}_2$
From the products, $Y$ is the base $M\text{OH}$, $Z$ is hydrogen peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$), and $W$ is the diatomic gas oxygen ($\text{O}_2$).

Calculating the atomicity of each:
Atomicity of $Y$ ($M\text{OH}$) = $1 + 1 + 1 = 3$
Atomicity of $Z$ ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) = $2 + 2 = 4$
Atomicity of $W$ ($\text{O}_2$) = $2$

The sum of their atomicities is $3 + 3 + 4 + 2 = 12$.

Answer: $12$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkali metals is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution, and what is the primary thermodynamic factor responsible for this behavior?
questions.question: Which of the following alkali metals is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution, and what is the primary thermodynamic factor responsible for this behavior?
options: $\text{Cs}$, due to its lowest ionization enthalpy
$\text{Li}$, due to its lowest ionization enthalpy
$\text{Na}$, due to its highest hydration enthalpy
$\text{Li}$, due to its highest hydration enthalpy
questions.solution:
In aqueous solution, the reducing power of an alkali metal is determined by its standard electrode potential ($E^\circ$). The overall standard free energy change depends on three factors: sublimation enthalpy, ionization enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy.

Although Lithium ($\text{Li}$) has the highest ionization enthalpy among alkali metals, its small ionic size results in an exceptionally high hydration enthalpy. This large release of energy during hydration more than compensates for the high energy required for ionization, making its standard reduction potential the most negative.

Therefore, $\text{Li}$ is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution primarily because of its highest hydration enthalpy.

Answer: $\text{Li}$, due to its highest hydration enthalpy

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Four elements are designated as P, Q, R, and S with atomic numbers 8, 12, 13, and 19 respectively. Which of the following represents the correct increasing order of their metallic character?
questions.question: Four elements are designated as P, Q, R, and S with atomic numbers 8, 12, 13, and 19 respectively. Which of the following represents the correct increasing order of their metallic character?
questions.solution:
The elements are identified by their atomic numbers:
P ($Z = 8$) is Oxygen (Group 16, Period 2).
Q ($Z = 12$) is Magnesium (Group 2, Period 3).
R ($Z = 13$) is Aluminium (Group 13, Period 3).
S ($Z = 19$) is Potassium (Group 1, Period 4).

Metallic character decreases across a period from left to right and increases down a group.
Oxygen is a non-metal and has the least metallic character.
Between Magnesium and Aluminium (same period), Magnesium is more metallic because it is further to the left in the periodic table.
Potassium is in Group 1 and Period 4, making it the most metallic among the given elements.

Thus, the increasing order of metallic character is Oxygen $<$ Aluminium $<$ Magnesium $<$ Potassium.
This corresponds to $P < R < Q < S$.

Answer: $P < R < Q < S$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The density of potassium is less than that of sodium because the increase in atomic volume from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{K}$ is disproportionately larger than the increase in atomic mass.

Statement II: The melting points of alkali metals increase down the group due to the increasing strength of metallic bonding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The density of potassium is less than that of sodium because the increase in atomic volume from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{K}$ is disproportionately larger than the increase in atomic mass.

Statement II: The melting points of alkali metals increase down the group due to the increasing strength of metallic bonding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution:
Statement I is true. While moving from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{K}$, the atomic mass increases, but the atomic volume increases disproportionately, making potassium lighter than sodium.

Statement II is false. The melting points of alkali metals decrease down the group. This is because as the atomic size increases, the strength of the metallic bond weakens, requiring less thermal energy to break the lattice.

Hence, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Element $\text{P}$ is a Group $1$ metal whose ion has the maximum magnitude of hydration enthalpy in its group. Element $\text{Q}$ is a Group $2$ metal whose ion has the maximum magnitude of hydration enthalpy in its group. Element $\text{P}$ exhibits a diagonal relationship with an element $\text{R}$. The identities of elements $\text{R}$ and $\text{Q}$, respectively, are
questions.question: Element $\text{P}$ is a Group $1$ metal whose ion has the maximum magnitude of hydration enthalpy in its group. Element $\text{Q}$ is a Group $2$ metal whose ion has the maximum magnitude of hydration enthalpy in its group. Element $\text{P}$ exhibits a diagonal relationship with an element $\text{R}$. The identities of elements $\text{R}$ and $\text{Q}$, respectively, are
questions.solution:
The magnitude of hydration enthalpy is inversely proportional to the ionic size.

In Group $1$, the $\text{Li}^{+}$ ion is the smallest, so Lithium ($\text{Li}$) has the maximum magnitude of hydration enthalpy. Thus, element $\text{P}$ is $\text{Li}$.

In Group $2$, the $\text{Be}^{2+}$ ion is the smallest, so Beryllium ($\text{Be}$) has the maximum magnitude of hydration enthalpy. Thus, element $\text{Q}$ is $\text{Be}$.

Lithium ($\text{P}$) exhibits a diagonal relationship with Magnesium ($\text{Mg}$) in Group $2$. Therefore, element $\text{R}$ is $\text{Mg}$.

The identities of elements $\text{R}$ and $\text{Q}$, respectively, are $\text{Mg}$ and $\text{Be}$.

Answer: $\text{Mg}$ and $\text{Be}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solid mixture containing $4\text{ moles}$ of $\text{LiNO}_3$, $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NaNO}_3$, $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3$ and $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is heated strongly to a constant weight. The total number of moles of gas(es) evolved is ________.
questions.question: A solid mixture containing $4\text{ moles}$ of $\text{LiNO}_3$, $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NaNO}_3$, $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3$ and $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is heated strongly to a constant weight. The total number of moles of gas(es) evolved is ________.
questions.solution:
Let us write the balanced thermal decomposition reactions for each compound in the mixture:

1. Lithium nitrate decomposes to give lithium oxide, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen:
$4\text{LiNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{Li}_2\text{O} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$
From $4\text{ moles}$ of $\text{LiNO}_3$, we get $4\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NO}_2$ and $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{O}_2$.
Moles of gas from $\text{LiNO}_3$ = $4 + 1 = 5\text{ moles}$.

2. Sodium nitrate decomposes to give sodium nitrite and oxygen:
$2\text{NaNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{O}_2$
From $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{NaNO}_3$, we get $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{O}_2$.
Moles of gas from $\text{NaNO}_3$ = $1\text{ mole}$.

3. Lithium carbonate decomposes to give lithium oxide and carbon dioxide:
$\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Li}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$
From $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3$, we get $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{CO}_2$.
Moles of gas from $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3$ = $2\text{ moles}$.

4. Sodium carbonate ($\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$) is thermally stable and does not decompose on heating.
Moles of gas from $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ = $0$.

Total moles of gas evolved = $5 + 1 + 2 + 0 = 8$.

Answer: $8$

questions.q:
Consider the following list of oxides:
$Na_2O$, $Tl_2O$, $B_2O_3$, $Al_2O_3$, $CO$, $NO$, $N_2O$, $Cl_2O_7$, $ZnO$

The number of neutral, amphoteric, and acidic oxides in the given list respectively are:
questions.question:
Consider the following list of oxides:
$Na_2O$, $Tl_2O$, $B_2O_3$, $Al_2O_3$, $CO$, $NO$, $N_2O$, $Cl_2O_7$, $ZnO$

The number of neutral, amphoteric, and acidic oxides in the given list respectively are:
questions.solution:
Let us classify each oxide in the given list:

1. $Na_2O$: Alkali metal oxide → Basic
2. $Tl_2O$: Lower oxidation state metal oxide of group 13 → Basic
3. $B_2O_3$: Non-metal/metalloid oxide → Acidic
4. $Al_2O_3$: Metal oxide → Amphoteric
5. $CO$: Non-metal oxide → Neutral
6. $NO$: Non-metal oxide → Neutral
7. $N_2O$: Non-metal oxide → Neutral
8. $Cl_2O_7$: Non-metal oxide in high oxidation state → Acidic
9. $ZnO$: Metal oxide → Amphoteric

Counting the categories:
Neutral oxides ($CO$, $NO$, $N_2O$) = 3
Amphoteric oxides ($Al_2O_3$, $ZnO$) = 2
Acidic oxides ($B_2O_3$, $Cl_2O_7$) = 2

The required sequence is 3, 2, 2.

Answer: 3, 2, 2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are four statements regarding s-block elements:


(A) The hydration enthalpy of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ is more negative than that of $\text{Na}^+$.
(B) The aqueous ionic mobility of alkali metals follows the order $\text{Cs}^+ > \text{Rb}^+ > \text{K}^+ > \text{Na}^+ > \text{Li}^+$.
(C) The hydrated radius of $\text{Be}^{2+}$ is smaller than that of $\text{Ba}^{2+}$.
(D) The magnitude of hydration enthalpy decreases down the group for alkaline earth metals.


Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Given below are four statements regarding s-block elements:


(A) The hydration enthalpy of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ is more negative than that of $\text{Na}^+$.
(B) The aqueous ionic mobility of alkali metals follows the order $\text{Cs}^+ > \text{Rb}^+ > \text{K}^+ > \text{Na}^+ > \text{Li}^+$.
(C) The hydrated radius of $\text{Be}^{2+}$ is smaller than that of $\text{Ba}^{2+}$.
(D) The magnitude of hydration enthalpy decreases down the group for alkaline earth metals.


Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct: Alkaline earth metal ions like $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ have a higher charge and smaller size than alkali metal ions like $\text{Na}^+$, leading to a higher charge density and a more negative hydration enthalpy.

Statement (B) is correct: Smaller bare ions are more extensively hydrated. Thus, $\text{Li}^+$ has the largest hydrated radius and consequently the lowest ionic mobility in aqueous solution, while $\text{Cs}^+$ has the highest ionic mobility.

Statement (C) is incorrect: Due to its very small bare ionic size, $\text{Be}^{2+}$ is heavily hydrated, making its hydrated radius much larger than that of the larger $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ ion.

Statement (D) is correct: As bare ionic size increases down the group, the extent of hydration decreases, causing the magnitude of hydration enthalpy to decrease.

Therefore, statements (A), (B) and (D) are correct.

Answer: (A), (B) and (D) only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following alkaline earth metals in the increasing order of their density:
$\text{Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba}$
questions.question:
Arrange the following alkaline earth metals in the increasing order of their density:
$\text{Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba}$
questions.solution:
The density of alkaline earth metals does not show a regular trend down the group. From $\text{Be}$ to $\text{Ca}$, the density decreases because the increase in atomic volume is more prominent than the increase in atomic mass. However, from $\text{Ca}$ to $\text{Ba}$, the density increases as the increase in atomic mass outweighs the increase in atomic volume.

The actual densities (in $\text{g/cm}^3$) are approximately: $\text{Be}$ ($1.84$), $\text{Mg}$ ($1.74$), $\text{Ca}$ ($1.55$), $\text{Sr}$ ($2.63$), and $\text{Ba}$ ($3.59$).

Therefore, the correct increasing order of density is $\text{Ca} < \text{Mg} < \text{Be} < \text{Sr} < \text{Ba}$.

Answer: $\text{Ca} < \text{Mg} < \text{Be} < \text{Sr} < \text{Ba}$
